text:
alex: FYI ran nightly perf pass on Qwen+Mixtral long‑seq traffic — saw RoPE scale shift trigger kernel fallback and ~18% p95 latency regression. attaching quick profiler dump.
maya: can you paste the profiler snip? curious if it's kernel selection or KV thrash.
alex: here — pasted minimal snapshot below. this is from the top of the trace where latency jumps and batcher grows.
```
PROFILE SNAPSHOT:
model_family: qwen-32k / mixtral-8x
workload: long-seq (avg len 4096, 50% > 6k)
baseline p50/p95 tokens/sec: 2300 / 1100
current p50/p95 tokens/sec: 2100 / 900
p95 latency: 220ms -> 260ms (+18%)
KV cache hit-rate: 98% -> 92% (spike in misses correlated w/ large prefixes)
kernel selection sequence:
  - warmup: matmul_v2_fp8_opt
  - regression region: matmul_int8_gemm (fallback path)
batcher: dynamic_adaptive microbatch target: 4 -> observed 6 (queueing increase)
device util: GPU SM util 72% -> 86% during regression window
trace hint: RoPE_scale_factor changed from 1.0 -> 1.15 for long offsets, which coincides with kernel switch
```
sam: looks like kernel selector flips to the int8 gemm when the RoPE scale expands effective head dims; that can change tiling heuristics and push microbatch growth. KV miss uptick suggests prefetch policy no longer covering the longer effective stride.
maya: @sam can you propose a quick mitigation we can test on canary?
sam: two quick experiments: 1) force kernel_policy=prefer_fp8 for qwen/mixtral family to avoid fallback; 2) sample adaptive_prefetch.window=8192 and lower adaptive_prefetch.evict_threshold to reduce KV thrash. both cheap to try. example config: 
```json
{"kernel_policy":"prefer_fp8","adaptive_prefetch":{"window":8192,"evict_threshold":0.6}}
```
jordan: note on quant side — when we force fp8 kernels, AWQ & GPTQ profiles diverge on some prompts. alex: did you run eval set after forcing policy?
alex: quick diff: forcing fp8 recovers p95 to ~230ms and tokens/sec ~1080, but AWQ calibrated checkpoint shows a +0.8% accuracy delta (slot-filling F1 drop) on our long-prefix calibration set. small but notable.
jordan: that matches expectation — quant kernels affect numeric path. try re-running AWQ calibration with extended prefix prompts (include long context tails). sample command I used: 
```bash
./quant-tool calibrate --model mixtral-8x --method awq --prompts-file=calib_longprefix.json --ropescale-aware
```
where calib_longprefix contains ~200 prompts with >3k token prefixes.
perf-bot: nightly-run 1738456000: regression detected for service=redwood-runtime, models=[qwen-32k,mixtral-8x], creating issue INF-4872; attached trace bucket s3://perf-traces/1738456123.tar.gz :robot_face:
maya: filing INF-4872, linking trace + eval diff + config snippet. also adding a canary run to dedicated pool with forced policy and adjusted prefetch.
alex: after canary run I'll post the small perf log, and if fp8 + recalib recovers accuracy, we can roll a short-term kernel pin while we refine selector heuristics.
sam: long term fix: update kernel selector cost model to include RoPE-induced tiling delta and add a prefetch sampling probe when sequence lengths shift. I can prod a PR for selector heuristics + a small mem-probe.
maya: ack. priority high because this affects any long-context customers. :exclamation:
jordan: one more note — run an INT8 vs FP8 microbenchmark for head_kv combos (heads=32/64, kv_dim=128/256) to map where selector flips. I have a bench script I can drop in the issue.
alex: thanks everyone — will run the canary now and update in this thread. :thumbsup:
